For he had spent three days without eating or drinking or speaking to us, or even turning from one side to the other. Instead, he lay like the dead in the large cell.
On the night of the twelfth of the month of Epip, someone called, “John!” I answered, “Bless me.”
He said to me, “I have drawn near to my end, and I will finish my course tomorrow at sunset, on the thirteenth.
But be careful: do not let anyone take my body away from the place I had dug for myself.
During these three days that I have spent without speaking to you, I have been standing before God, and my account has been taken since the ninth hour yesterday.
I say that God will show me his mercy.”
I said to him, “Please, my father, take a little food, for it has been four days since you tasted anything.”
My father answered me, “My son, shall I eat anything again after the accounting?
I tell you, I will not taste any food belonging to this world
until I go to Christ and break my fast in his presence.”
When day dawned on the thirteenth of Epip,
he said to me, while other prominent men were sitting beside him, “John, you know all my affairs: I have kept nothing belonging to the bishopric of the city of Coptos in my possession.
I have only one gold solidus of full weight, which I have had since the day I settled in my cell as a monk.
I earned it through the work of my hands and have kept it until the day when I would clothe my body through the work of my own hands, so that I would not leave a reproach for those who come after me,
and they say, ‘You have gone beyond what is proper.’
But you, John, use it to buy a covering for my body, and do not put anything else on me.”
Except for the tunic in which I was clothed, my monastic habit, my cowl, my belt, and my cloak alone, wrap me and bury me.
And I think: look, the field has been enclosed.
And look, the place has become full of wolves, because the fence has been thrown down. Everyone will do as he pleases.
But whatever each person does, no one will rebuke him, because the fences have been thrown down.
When our holy father Apa Pisenthius, the holy bishop, had said these things, he stopped [?] speaking with us.
He opened his mouth and gave his spirit into God's hands at sunset on the thirteenth of Epip, in the fifth year.
We lifted up his holy body and brought it into the holy sanctuary of the community at Tsenti.
We wrapped him according to the instructions he had given us.
We spent the whole night reading around him.
Afterward, we celebrated the Eucharistic offering over him.
We took him to the mountain where he had had us dig while he stood among us.
We buried him on the fourteenth of this same month, Epip, in the peace of God. Amen. [?]
Written in Thoth, in the fourth indiction, in year 722 of the holy martyrs, year [?].
I, Victor, the least of deacons, son of the late Mercurius the deacon, son of the late Eponychus, archdeacon of Saint Mercurius the great commander, from
the city of Latopolis, wrote this book. May everyone who reads this book pray for me, so that the Lord may guide my wretched life to become pleasing to him. Amen.
Through the zeal and care of our God-loving, beloved brothers, Michael the archdeacon and [?],
and our brother Zechariah, the second deacon and monk of Saint Mercurius the commander, whose monastery is on the mountain of Edfu,

they prepared this book and placed it in their monastery so that it might be read for the benefit and assurance of those who listen attentively. May the Lord Jesus Christ grant them a long life and endurance.
May he save them from the snares of the devil and from evil people.
May he place blessing, abundance, and salvation in their monastery.
May he preserve the life of our father, the superior Abba Abraham, and the whole assembly of cross-bearing brothers who live in their monastery, each one by name.
May he send their holy blessing down upon my lowliness. When they depart from the body, may they receive an inheritance with the fathers of the community: Apa Pachomius,
and Apa Theodore, and Apa Palamon, and Apa Petronius, and Apa Horsiesius, and all the fathers of the community. Amen. May it be so for us all. Amen.
